newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares boosted by Mideast, Iraq hopes.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares boosted by Mideast, Iraq hopes.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose for the first time in a week on Tuesday, climbing 0.22 percent on hopes that Palestinians and Israelis may be closing gaps in their long talks over troop redeployment in Hebron.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.33 points to 147.87 points, reversing a shallow slide over the last 10 days after renewed activity in a few select stocks, brokers said.

"There was a feeling this morning that a peace agreement might be reached soon between the Israelis and the Palestinians," said one broker on the Amman exchange, which is highly sensitive to regional politics.
"This really had a positive effect on investors," he said.
News that Jordan had agreed to supply sanction-hit Iraq with an extra $35 million of vegetable oil, soap and detergents also gave the exchange a much needed shot in the arm.
Vegetable oil producer Universal Modern Industries Corp soared five percent to 1.60 dinars from 1.52 dinars in trade worth 38,600 dinars, worth nearly 10 percent of Tuesday's 410,000 dinar turnover.

The company, hit by cuts in sales to Iraq since sanctions were imposed in 1990 and by a flood of high quality vegetable oil from neighbouring Saudi Arabia, was expected to benefit most from the extra supplies to Baghdad, brokers said.
Heavy trade for a second day running in the Middle East Investment Bank also boosted turnover.
The bank, expected to make a private share placement with a French bank, closed unchanged at 1.10 dinars after shares worth 84,000 dinars were traded.
A private index by Pearl Consulting of Amman's 45 most prominent shares rose 0.07 percent on Tuesday to 80.21 percent, still 16.02 percent lower than a year before.
Overall 16 shares rose and 11 fell, with another 19 trading but closing unchanged.
